# Final capstone

The end of the course is a launch point, not a finish line. Red-coder training
means repeated cycles of contest, upsolve, proof cleanup, and template review.
The capstone mixes subset search, congruence modeling, and recurrence speed.

## What "red-coder training" means

At this level, improvement is less about learning isolated algorithms and more
about reducing recognition time, proof time, and implementation risk.

A weekly cycle:

```text
1. One serious contest or virtual contest.
2. Full upsolve of every missed problem near your range.
3. Rewrite one proof cleanly.
4. Stress-test one implementation.
5. Add one pattern to your notebook.
```

## Capstone A: meet-in-the-middle

Maximum subset sum not exceeding `X` should trigger:

```text
n around 40 -> split into two halves
enumerate sums -> sort one side -> binary search complement
```

The proof is that every subset is uniquely the union of a left-half subset and
a right-half subset.

## Capstone B: CRT

Merging congruences should trigger:

```text
x = a mod m
x = b mod n
check gcd compatibility
merge into x = c mod lcm(m,n)
```

The compatibility check is not optional. If residues disagree modulo the gcd,
there is no integer satisfying both.

## Capstone C: fast recurrence

Many recurrence problems are solved by matrix exponentiation. Fibonacci has a
special fast-doubling form:

```text
(F(n), F(n+1)) -> (F(2n), F(2n+1))
```

The habit to keep is not memorizing Fibonacci only; it is recognizing when a
linear recurrence needs logarithmic exponentiation.

## Final self-review rubric

For each problem you solve after this course, ask:

- Did I identify the model before coding?
- Did I state the invariant or recurrence?
- Did I prove the transition?
- Did I test the smallest and largest meaningful cases?
- Did I preserve a reusable lesson for the next contest?

That loop is how this course continues after the final PDF.

## Capstone integration drill

When opening a hard problem, write a three-column scratch table:

```text
Observed constraint | Possible model | Why it might fit
n <= 40             | MITM           | split exponential search
mod equations       | CRT            | merge congruences
linear recurrence   | matrix/doubling| logarithmic query
tree all roots      | rerooting      | answer for every root
range updates       | lazy segtree   | update/query intervals
```

Then eliminate models whose assumptions fail. This habit is what turns a large
course into contest speed.

## Final implementation rule

For red-level problems, never start from the longest template. Start from the
smallest correct skeleton that proves the model:

```text
parse
build the compressed state
answer one query
test tiny cases
only then optimize or generalize
```

## Final practice protocol

For the next 20 virtual contests:

```text
Before contest: choose one focus skill.
During contest: write model/invariant before each medium+ problem.
After contest: upsolve until every official solution is understandable.
After upsolve: rewrite one solution without looking.
Weekly: review failed patterns and update the notebook.
```

The course gives you the map. This protocol turns the map into reflexes.

## What to maintain after the course

Keep three artifacts:

```text
template notebook: trusted implementation snippets
pattern notebook: observations that unlock problems
mistake notebook: bugs you have personally made
```

The mistake notebook matters most. Red-coder progress often comes from not
making the same wrong assumption twice.

## Final capstone self-test

Before considering the course complete, take one problem from each category and
solve it without looking at the lesson:

```text
Fenwick/segment tree query
shortest path or flow model
tree DP or rerooting
string matching/hash
number theory/combinatorics
game or invariant problem
```

The target is not memorization; it is recognizing which model the statement is
trying to hide.

# Exercises

- A. Capstone Subset: Meet-in-the-middle: maximum subset sum not exceeding `X`.
- B. Capstone CRT: Merge pairs of congruences or report impossibility.
- C. Capstone Recurrence: Fast Fibonacci queries modulo `1e9+7`.
# Contest checklist

State the invariant, choose the model, prove the operation, then code the smallest reliable version.
